newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso down 3 pesos amid speculation.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso down 3 pesos amid speculation.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed three pesos down at 1,078.5 against the dollar in a session driven by speculation, interbank traders said.

"There weren't many greenbacks flowing into the markets except petrodollars and we expect there may be some price correction tomorrow," one dealer said. Dealers suggested the speculative wave may have been driven by a central bank decision to impose a "reserve requirement" on all new foreign loans, regardless of the pay-back period. Borrowers will have to deposit 30 percent of the value of their loan in pesos with the central bank for 18 months. At the end of that period the deposit will be repaid with no interest accrued.
The move is seen as a way of discouraging foreign loans and thereby helping to devalue the peso within the central bank target area of between 15 percent and 29 percent.
Dealers reported 416 trades worth a total $210 million, above the daily average of about $180 million. The peso hit an intraday high of 1,076.8 and sank to an intraday low of 1,083.5.
